notes: Reconciled from coder A and coder B. Coded four included documents. The university-wide AI policy is an information-security policy; coursework is delegated to the Academic Integrity Policy and instructor syllabus statements. Two ECE uses (literature search, concept illustrations) were UNCOVERED. | Coder B. Rowan has no university-wide academic-use AI policy (Faculty Center says so); the university AI Policy is an information-security rule. No school-level document found. The deferred instructor syllabus and the irt-aipolicy cached text were not coded because they are not included in the collect file. Data-analysis bans (2 units, ECE) were left UNCOVERED because P89 only covers the permit side; a candidate type is a ban on AI for data analysis or interpretation. Literature search and concept-figure permissions are also UNCOVERED. | Reconciler: dropped one-coder units that only describe external links or resources (A: 'How to cite the use of AI', two Elon field-guide blurbs, plus the library-guide counterparts; B: the Montclair 'no software is able to detect AI-generated content with 100% certainty' link blurb). Candidate new type: a ban on AI for data analysis or interpretation of results (two ECE units are UNCOVERED, mirror of P89). Candidate UNCOVERED: AI for literature search and AI-generated concept figures (two ECE units). The irt-aipolicy text was not coded because it is not in the collect file. Course layer deferred.

documents.unit: Division of Information Resources & Technology and Office of the Provost
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Policy (University Policies)
documents.summary: An information-security policy for the whole university. It bans putting confidential data into public AI tools, limits university business to approved platforms, and covers AI recording, procurement, copyright and research. On coursework it only says to follow the Academic Integrity Policy.
documents.stance_why: The policy is an information-security rule: it limits what data may enter AI tools and requires approved platforms for university business. It sets no stance on students' use of AI in coursework and sends coursework to the Academic Integrity Policy, so the stance is delegates. The words "AI requirements related to coursework must comply with the Academic Integrity Policy" show this.

units.resolution_why: Disagreement on actor: actor A=admin B=all. Purpose sentence of a university-wide information-security policy that applies to the whole Rowan community; it is not addressed to administrators alone, so actor is all.
units.why: The sentence sets the policy purpose: "establish requirements for the secure use of AI and Large Language Models". It states purpose and scope, so it is an institution-level framework (P56) rather than a rule on coursework.
units.anchor: establish requirements for the secure use of AI and Large Language Models

units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this. The source says the CIO, Information Security Officer and Provost 'shall ensure compliance with this policy', a real accountability rule (P80, admin, must). Kept.
units.why: The Provost and security officers "shall ensure compliance" with the policy; this names who owns and enforces it, so P80 rather than P56.
units.anchor: shall ensure compliance with this policy

units.why: "The Vice Presidents and Deans shall implement this policy" assigns implementation to named officers, which is P80 (who owns the policy).
units.anchor: The Vice Presidents and Deans shall implement this policy

units.why: This sets who the policy binds: "all members of the Rowan Community who access and use the University's electronic information and information systems". It is scope, so P56.
units.anchor: applies to all members of the Rowan Community

units.why: "The use of AI tools must adhere to all Rowan University policies" requires AI use to follow existing university policy, which is P77 (comply with existing policy), not P45.
units.anchor: The use of AI tools must adhere to all Rowan University policies

units.why: Members "must adhere to ... ethical standards and policies of the University, with regard to data use, privacy, consent, ownership, and academic integrity", tying AI use to existing law and policy: P77.
units.anchor: must adhere to human resource and legal requirements, as well as ethical standards and policies
units.policy: must adhere to human resource and legal requirements, as well as ethical standards and policies of the University

units.why: Employees "should be aware of the requirements of the Open Public Records Act" and that AI meeting transcripts may be public records. This is a legal-compliance duty (P77); P86 does not fit because it is about consent to record, not records law.
units.anchor: AI generated transcripts of meetings may create records subject to OPRA
units.fit_note: Also touches AI meeting transcription, but the point is public-records law.

units.why: "must not enter Rowan internal, confidential, proprietary or regulated data ... into publicly-available AI tools, e.g. ChatGPT" bans a class of input to AI, to protect data: P50 (protect confidential data) fits better than P20, which is about assignment specs and student code.
units.anchor: must not enter Rowan internal, confidential, proprietary or regulated data
units.policy: Members of the Rowan community must not enter Rowan internal, confidential, proprietary or regulated data (finance, PII, ePHI, HR, student records, non-public research data) into publicly-available AI tools

units.why: "must only be processed in officially approved AI/LLM platforms" requires university business, including academic communications, to use approved tools; that is P92 (use approved tools institution-wide).
units.anchor: must only be processed in officially approved AI/LLM platforms

units.why: "No University business information may be processed on any unapproved platform" is a flat ban on unapproved platforms for university business, justified by data discoverability; coded P92 as the same approved-tools rule.
units.anchor: No University business information may be processed on any unapproved platform

units.resolution_why: Disagreement on actor: actor A=admin B=all. Procurement rule binds anyone who buys AI subscriptions, not only administrators; the source says 'Subscriptions and purchases of AI services must be procured through the standard processes', so actor is all.
units.why: "Subscriptions and purchases of AI services must be procured through the standard processes" of IRT and Contracting sets institutional control before purchase: P65.
units.anchor: Subscriptions and purchases of AI services must be procured through the standard processes

units.resolution_why: Disagreement on phase: phase A=general B=during-work. A said phase general, B said during-work. The rule is about recording workplace meetings, not assignments or studying, so general (A) follows the phase definitions.
units.why: The sentence 'Internal and closed meetings may only be recorded by AI platforms that are authorized, secured and managed by IRT' limits which platform may record meetings. It is not coursework or study, so phase is general. Everyone who records meetings is bound, modality is must, and P86 (recording and transcription) is the nearest type.
units.anchor: Internal and closed meetings may only be recorded by AI platforms that are authorized
units.fit_note: Condition is IRT authorization, not consent of participants. | Requires IRT authorization of the recording platform rather than consent of participants.

units.resolution_why: Disagreement on actor, phase: actor A=all B=ta-staff; phase A=general B=during-work. A said actor all and phase general; B said ta-staff and during-work. The source addresses no particular role and concerns confidential HR meetings, not assignments, so all and general.
units.why: The passage 'AI transcriptions of confidential Human Resources meetings, including candidate interviews, should not be used' applies to anyone who would transcribe an HR meeting, and it is not coursework, so actor is all and phase is general. 'Should not be used' gives should-not and P86 is the nearest type (AI recording and transcription).
units.anchor: AI transcriptions of confidential Human Resources meetings, including candidate interviews, should not be used

units.resolution_why: Disagreement on actor: actor A=student B=all. A said actor student, B said all. 'AI requirements related to coursework must comply with the Academic Integrity Policy' binds everyone doing or supervising coursework, and the policy is university-wide, so all.
units.why: "AI requirements related to coursework must comply with the Academic Integrity Policy" sends coursework AI rules to the existing integrity policy rather than setting a rule: P77 (comply with existing policy).
units.anchor: AI requirements related to coursework must comply with the Academic Integrity Policy
units.fit_note: Also shows the policy leaves coursework AI rules to the Academic Integrity Policy and instructors.

units.why: "Questions regarding the use of AI or data mining tools should be directed to the ... Office of Ethics, Academic Integrity or Research" names the offices that field questions about the policy: P80.
units.anchor: Questions regarding the use of AI or data mining tools should be directed to
units.policy: Questions about AI or data mining tools go to the Rowan University Office of Ethics, Academic Integrity or Research, as appropriate
units.fit_note: Names where users ask questions, not who interprets or enforces.

units.why: "The use of AI may not infringe on copyright laws" with the University Copyright Policy is a rule on copyright of AI use: P52.
units.anchor: The use of AI may not infringe on copyright laws

units.why: "AI use in Research ... must be conducted in accordance with applicable policies and governing Research" defers research AI to existing research rules, which is P62.
units.anchor: AI use in Research, including the development of AI and other machine learning, must be
units.policy: AI use in Research, including the development of AI and other machine learning, must be conducted in accordance with applicable policies

units.why: "shall be subject to discipline up to and including dismissal" states the consequence of violating the policy. P37 (state penalties in advance) fits partly because the penalty is for violating a data-security policy.
units.anchor: shall be subject to discipline up to and including dismissal from the University
units.fit_note: Penalties apply to any violator of this security policy, mostly employees, not students' academic misconduct. | Penalty is for violating the data-security policy, not for academic AI misuse.

units.why: "Any exceptions to this policy must be approved by the Information Security Office and Office of the Provost" names who grants exceptions: P80.
units.anchor: exceptions to this policy must be approved by the Information Security Office and Office of
units.policy: exceptions to this policy must be approved by the Information Security Office and Office of the Provost

documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence & Teaching
tiers: Option 1: No generative AI (violation of academic integrity)
Option 2: No generative AI (assignments are for developing and assessing skills)
Option 3: Some generative AI (support learning, cite, work must be the student's own)
Option 4: Generic statement (follow instructor guidelines; cite; unauthorized use may be cheating)
documents.summary: Faculty Center page that says Rowan has no universal GenAI policy, recommends a syllabus statement and offers four sample statements from no AI to some AI. It also gives advice on detectors, citations and follow-up with students, plus many resource links.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'The University does not have a universal generative AI policy' and offers sample statements instead, with Option 4 saying 'you must follow all instructor guidelines'. Because it provides templates and leaves the choice to instructors, the stance is delegates with the tiers listed.

units.resolution_why: Disagreement on phase: phase A=course-start B=before-course. A said phase course-start, B said before-course. The sentence asks faculty to state in the syllabus and Canvas how AI may be used, which is communicating expectations, so course-start (A).
units.why: A University Senate task force recommendation that faculty 'include a clear and specific statement in their syllabi and Canvas', i.e. an AI statement in every syllabus (P09); it is 'should', not 'must'.
units.anchor: Faculty should include a clear and specific statement in their syllabi and Canvas

units.why: Points to a page on 'Rowan-licensed GenAI tools and guidelines', university-wide approved tools (P92); it is institution-wide, so not P17.
units.anchor: an overview of Rowan-licensed GenAI tools and guidelines for using them

units.resolution_why: Disagreement on actor, phase: actor A=all B=instructor; phase A=general B=before-course. A said actor all and phase general, B said instructor and before-course. 'The University does not have a universal generative AI policy' is a fact about the whole institution, not an instruction to instructors, so all and general (A).
units.why: Says no single university rule exists and leaves it to instructors ('Instructors may select one of the following statements'), which is letting the instructor set the rule (P04).
units.anchor: The University does not have a universal generative AI policy.

units.resolution_why: Disagreement on modality: modality A=may B=informs. A said modality may (B informs). 'Instructors may select one of the following statements if appropriate to their classroom' grants an option, so may (A).
units.why: Offers a menu of four sample syllabus statements from 'No generative AI' to 'Some generative AI', which are templates at different levels of use (P05).
units.anchor: Instructors may select one of the following statements if appropriate to their classroom.
units.fit_note: Options are sample wording, not formally named tiers.

units.resolution_why: Disagreement on phase: phase A=during-work B=general. A said phase during-work, B said general. The Option 1 text governs what students do in the course ('In this course, any use of generative artificial intelligence ... '), so during-work.
units.why: Option 1 sample statement: 'any use of generative artificial intelligence ... will be considered a violation of academic integrity'. It bans AI in the course, so must-not, prohibit and P01. It applies to the work students do in the course, so phase is during-work.
units.anchor: any use of generative artificial intelligence such as ChatGPT, DALL-E, Claude, Copilot, Gemini, and others
units.policy: any use of generative artificial intelligence such as ChatGPT, DALL-E, Claude, Copilot, Gemini, and others will be considered a violation of academic integrity

units.why: Lists sanctions in advance ('fail the assignment, fail the course, or face other sanctions') in the Option 1 text: concrete penalties (P37).
units.anchor: students committing any act of academic dishonesty may fail the assignment, fail the course

units.why: A procedural duty ('must be reported to the Provost's Office') once a penalty is given, the formal integrity-reporting procedure (P81).
units.anchor: Violations that result in a grade penalty must be reported to the Provost's Office.

units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded this. Option 1 says 'students should provide appropriate documentation whenever quoting, paraphrasing, summarizing, or otherwise using the language or ideas of others', a citation rule in the sample statement. Kept as P24 with A's fit note.
units.why: Asks students to document use of 'the language or ideas of others', a general attribution rule inside the no-AI template (P24); it does not name AI, hence the fit note.
units.anchor: students should provide appropriate documentation whenever quoting, paraphrasing, summarizing
units.fit_note: Does not mention AI itself; general attribution advice in the Option 1 template.

units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded this. Option 2 states 'The purpose of the assignments in this course is to help you develop key skills'; it is the rationale for the ban, a real P41 statement. Kept.
units.why: Option 2 grounds the ban in assignments that 'help you develop key skills' and 'assess whether you have mastered', which explains that AI shortcuts skill-building practice (P41).
units.anchor: to help you develop key skills and to assess whether you have mastered

units.resolution_why: Disagreement on phase, modality, policy_type: phase A=during-work B=when-misuse; modality A=must-not B=informs; policy_type A=P01 B=P36. A coded P01 must-not prohibit; B coded P36 informs neutral (B7 coded the rationale clause separately as P41). The sentence sits under 'No generative AI' and says use 'defeats the purpose ... and is considered an academic integrity violation', which bans the use; a reader looking for the Option 2 ban expects P01. The purpose rationale is kept as its own P41 unit (B7).
units.why: Option 2 sample statement under the heading 'No generative AI': 'Using generative AI or other unauthorized tools on these assignments defeats the purpose'. The sentence bans AI on the assignments and calls it a violation, so must-not, prohibit and P01. The 'academic integrity violation' wording is part of the same ban, so one P01 unit covers it.
units.anchor: Using generative AI or other unauthorized tools on these assignments defeats the purpose
units.policy: Using generative AI or other unauthorized tools on these assignments defeats the purpose of the assignments, misrepresents the student's mastery of the material and is considered an academic integrity violation (Option 2 sample statement).

units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this. The Option 2 sentence says using AI 'defeats the purpose, misrepresents your mastery of the material'; it explains why AI misuse harms learning (P41). Kept; coder A's P41 unit covers the preceding purpose sentence.
units.why: Option 2 explains that unauthorized AI "defeats the purpose, misrepresents your mastery of the material" of the assignments, a skill-building rationale: P41 (chosen over P43 because the main claim is that AI shortcuts the practice).
units.anchor: defeats the purpose, misrepresents your mastery of the material

units.resolution_why: Disagreement on phase: phase A=during-work B=course-start. A said phase during-work, B said course-start. 'If you have questions about what resources may be allowed on a specific assignment please let me know' is triggered when a student weighs using a resource on an assignment, so during-work (A).
units.why: Option 2 tells students to ask the instructor when unsure about allowed resources ('please let me know'), which is P10.
units.anchor: what resources may be allowed on a specific assignment please let me know

units.why: Option 3 allows AI 'to support learning (e.g., in obtaining feedback or generating ideas)'. Ideas fits brainstorming (P15); feedback is not captured, so noted.
units.anchor: tool to support learning (e.g., in obtaining feedback or generating ideas)
units.fit_note: Also permits obtaining feedback, which P15 does not name. | Also permits AI for obtaining feedback, which no single type covers.

units.why: Option 3 requires submitted work to be the student's own, 'not the work of an AI system': the no-AI-produced-work rule (P19).
units.anchor: should be that of the student and not the work of an AI system

units.why: Option 3 says AI-generated material 'should be cited like any other reference material', a disclosure-by-citation rule (P24); the comparison to other references is secondary.
units.anchor: it should be cited like any other reference material

units.why: Option 3 puts responsibility for errors on the student ('bears responsibility for any inaccuracies'). Chosen P29 (owns what is submitted) over P31 because it assigns accountability, not a duty to verify.
units.anchor: the student bears responsibility for any inaccuracies or misinformation
units.fit_note: Names responsibility for AI inaccuracies; no instruction to verify.

units.resolution_why: Disagreement on phase: phase A=during-work B=course-start. A said phase during-work, B said course-start. 'please reach out to your instructor' concerns questions about how AI may be used to complete assignments, so during-work (A).
units.why: Option 3 asks students with questions about AI use to 'reach out to your instructor': ask before using (P10).
units.anchor: please reach out to your instructor

units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded this. Option 4 says 'it is possible for generative AI to be used as a tool to support learning', a statement in the sample syllabus text that states a benefit of AI for learning (P87). Kept.
units.why: Option 4 concedes AI 'can be used as a tool to support learning', which states a benefit of AI without making it a rule (P87).
units.anchor: it is possible for generative AI to be used as a tool to support learning

units.resolution_why: Disagreement on phase: phase A=course-start B=during-work. A said phase course-start, B said during-work. Option 4 says 'you must follow all instructor guidelines ... while completing assignments', so following the rules happens during-work (B).
units.why: The generic statement says students "must follow all instructor guidelines on the use or prohibition of generative AI", making each instructor's rule binding: P78 (follow each course's rules).
units.anchor: you must follow all instructor guidelines on the use or prohibition of generative AI
units.fit_note: Also delegates the stance to the instructor.

units.why: Option 4 classes 'unauthorized use of generative AI' as possible 'cheating' under the integrity policy, which is P36.
units.anchor: The unauthorized use of generative AI on assignments may be considered cheating

units.resolution_why: Disagreement on unit_stance: unit_stance A=permit B=restrict. A said unit_stance permit, B said restrict. 'Submitting the output of generative AI without citation is considered plagiarism' implies cited use is acceptable, which matches how both coders treated the Option 3 citation sentence (permit), so permit (A).
units.why: Option 4 makes missing citation the violation: 'without citation is considered plagiarism' (P28, nondisclosure as the violation).
units.anchor: Submitting the output of generative AI without citation is considered plagiarism

units.why: Option 4 repeats student responsibility ('you are responsible for any inaccuracies') for submitted work: P29.
units.anchor: you are responsible for any inaccuracies or information within your submitted assignments

units.resolution_why: Disagreement on phase: phase A=during-work B=course-start. A said phase during-work, B said course-start; the sentence invites students to ask the instructor for clarification when working on assignments, so during-work (A).
units.why: Option 4 invites students to ask the instructor for clarification, i.e. ask when unsure (P10).
units.anchor: please do not hesitate to reach out to your instructor for clarification

units.resolution_why: Disagreement on policy_type: policy_type A=P09 B=P04. A said P09 (require a syllabus statement), B said P04 (instructor sets the rule). 'Faculty also might choose to list the ways that generative AI could be used on some or all assignments' is optional and lets the instructor define permitted uses; P09 is about requiring a statement. So P04 (B).
units.why: "Faculty also might choose to list the ways that generative AI could be used on some or all assignments" lets instructors set the rule per assignment: P04.
units.anchor: Faculty also might choose to list the ways that generative AI could be used
units.fit_note: Optional advice to detail permitted uses; P09 is about a required statement.

units.why: Links a repository of other instructors' syllabus policies 'to help in the development of their own', faculty support for setting course policy (P63).
units.anchor: helping other instructors see the range of policies available by other educators

units.resolution_why: Disagreement on policy_type: policy_type A=P70 B=P66. A said P70 (training for students), B said P66 (explain the rules to students). The video 'Student Use of Generative AI' is a Rowan-produced resource to share with students; the page does not say it explains the rules, so the safer type is P70. The P66 reading is kept in fit_note.
units.why: A Rowan video on student AI use 'can be shown in class', material to explain AI rules to students: closest P70 (guides for students) though it also supports discussion (P66).
units.anchor: This Rowan-produced video (2:20) can be shown in class or linked in your Canvas
units.fit_note: Also supports explaining the rules in class (P66). | Offers a ready-made video rather than the instructor's own reasons.

units.resolution_why: Disagreement on actor, phase, unit_stance: actor A=student B=instructor; phase A=course-start B=before-course; unit_stance A=neutral B=encourage. A said actor student, B said instructor; A and B differed on unit_stance (neutral vs encourage). The page is addressed to faculty ('Faculty can add to their Canvas courses') and describes a resource without urging AI use, so instructor, informs, neutral.
units.why: 'Introduction to AI Literacy for Students is a Canvas module designed specifically for Rowan students' is an AI-literacy resource that the page offers to faculty, who can add it to their Canvas courses. units.anchor: Introduction to AI Literacy for Students is a Canvas module designed specifically for Rowan students

units.resolution_why: Disagreement on modality, unit_stance: modality A=informs B=may; unit_stance A=neutral B=encourage. A said modality informs, B said may and unit_stance encourage. units.why: Tells faculty 'we do NOT recommend relying on' AI content detectors, the do-not-rely-on-detectors type (P39).

units.policy: Such programs have not yet demonstrated their accuracy and do not provide hard evidence for evaluation

units.anchor: reports of false positives from these software systems that can lead to false accusations

documents.title: GenAI at Rowan: For Students
documents.summary: Student page of the library GenAI guide. It lists tools Rowan approves for data protection, warns that using GenAI without the instructor's permission may be an integrity violation, and links to citation guidance and student AI guides.

documents.title: Generative AI Use Policy
documents.date_or_term: cites AI tools accessed June-July 2025; no explicit date
documents.summary: A departmental policy for all undergraduate and graduate ECE courses. It welcomes AI for learning, brainstorming, debugging and proofreading, but not as the source of graded work, and lists banned uses, including code over 25 percent. It sets a detailed citation format and an oral or written check when misuse is suspected.
documents.stance_why: The ECE policy says it "welcomes, even encourages, responsible and educational use" of AI for learning, brainstorming and debugging, but only if AI content is not submitted as graded work; it allows up to 25% AI code and bans AI for answers, analysis, and reports. This is a permission with conditions and listed bans: permit.

units.anchor: ECE department welcomes, even encourages, responsible and educational use of Generative AI

units.why: "so long as the AI generated content is not submitted as graded work" is the limit on the welcome: AI may not produce submitted work. P19.
units.anchor: so long as the AI generated content is not submitted as graded work

units.policy: All students (and, in fact, all engineers) are ultimately responsible for describing, justifying and/or explaining their work
